summary: Embedded dashboard: URL filter parameters cause associated alerts to be suppressed intermittently
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that alerts tied to saved dashboard widgets are not firing when the dashboard is embedded with URL filter parameters. The alerts appear to evaluate without error in the alerting UI (green checks) but no incident notifications are generated for the filtered context.

Impact:
- Multiple Lumina Health monitoring dashboards did not trigger escalation for a threshold breach between 2026-03-09 22:10 and 2026-03-10 01:45 UTC.
- Potential compliance exposure for an enterprise healthcare customer because they rely on dashboard-driven alerts for SLA and Ops workflows.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east)
- Customer embedding dashboards via iframe with URL params (e.g., ?region=midwest&team=careflow)
- Alerts configured on dashboard saved queries (alert_eval window 1m, severity critical)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Save a dashboard with a widget alert on metric A (threshold > 5).
2. Embed dashboard in a customer page and append URL filters: ?region=us-east&team=ops
3. Trigger metric A to exceed threshold for >1 minute in the filtered scope.
4. Observe alert evaluation history and notification channel delivery.

Observed behavior:
- Alert evaluation logs show the alert checked and returned a state change timestamp but no incident or notification appears in the delivery channel (PagerDuty, email).
- When opening dashboard directly (no URL filters) alerts behave normally and fire notifications.
- Applying the same filter from dashboard UI (not via URL) also results in proper notifications.

Expected behavior:
- Alerts tied to dashboard queries should honor the exact filter context supplied via URL parameters for embedded dashboards and produce notifications when conditions are met.

Logs / links / artifacts:
- Customer-provided trace: https://s3.redwood-inference/test-exports/lumina/alert-eval-2026-03-10.log
- Internal trace link: https://traces.redwood.example/trace/7f3a2b
- Slack: #support thread <https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C05ABC12345/p164>
comments: 2026-03-10 09:17 - Aisha G (Support): Created ticket after Lumina Health reported missing notifications. Attached customer logs and reproduction steps.
2026-03-10 12:04 - Kenji S (Oncall SRE): Acknowledged. Marking P1. Initial hypothesis: URL filter context not being passed to alert eval pipeline, possible cache key mismatch in alerting-service.

2026-03-10 15:32 - Engineering (SRE): Reproduced locally using embedded iframe with URL params. Observed alert evaluation engine receives global filter instead of URL-scoped filters for embedded requests.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Kenji S (SRE): Added temporary alert rule-level fallback that forces evaluation to saved query parameters (workaround). Deployed to staging for validation.
2026-03-12 14:08 - Product (Maya Ortiz): Customer notified of in-progress fix and temporary mitigation. Coordinating release notes and postmortem scope.
investigation_notes: Checked alerting-service logs for eval window: alert-eval worker processed job id 0a3f at 2026-03-09T22:11:05Z.

Found discrepancy: requests originating from embedding proxy contain X-Embed-Filters header; alerting-service uses a cache key that only considers saved_query_id and org_id, ignoring X-Embed-Filters leading to stale cache hits.
Replication steps executed on staging: embedding proxy -> console-service -> alerting-service. Confirmed header dropped at console-service when request was transformed for background evaluation.

Hypothesis: recent refactor (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-service/commit/abc1234) removed propagation of embed filter context for background evals, resulting in alerting-service evaluating wrong filter set and de-duping notifications.

Observed that notification suppression occurs when an alert transitions back-and-forth within the same cache key period; because the evaluation used wrong filter, the system considered the state already seen and skipped notification deduping incorrectly.
root_cause: Console-service background evaluation path dropped embedded URL filter context (X-Embed-Filters header) after a refactor, causing alert eval cache keys to be computed without the embed-scoped filters. This led to false de-duplication and suppressed notifications for embedded dashboards.
resolution:
A patch was merged and deployed to prod that ensures console-service preserves embed filter headers for background alert evaluation and includes the embed filter fingerprint in the alerting-service cache key. The fix is in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-service/pull/4521 and deployed to us-east on 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC.

Workaround prior to patch: disable background evaluation for embedded dashboards (console toggle) or avoid URL-based embedding filters and use saved dashboard filters. We applied a temporary rule-level fallback that forces saved-query parameters while the patch rolled out.
postmortem_actions: 1) Backfill tests: add unit/integration tests to ensure X-Embed-Filters propagation across console-service background eval path.
2) Metric: add alert-eval telemetry to count cache key mismatches by source (embed vs console UI) and create a dashboard tile for 90-day trend.
3) Customer follow-up: schedule 1:1 with Lumina Health CS to review impact and provide evidence of fix and audit logs.
4) Runbook update: document embedding+alert evaluation interaction and mitigation steps in the Alert Evaluation Runbook.
public_communication: We have deployed a fix that addresses an issue where embedded dashboards with URL filters could suppress alert notifications. No further action is required from customers using embedded dashboards. Customers who previously used URL filters will see normal alerting behavior going forward. Affected customers were notified directly on 2026-03-12.
notes_for_support: If customer still sees missing notifications, ask for (1) dashboard id, (2) exact embed URL, (3) alert id, and (4) time window. Escalate to SRE oncall if missing after patch and provide trace link and request id.
expected_follow_up: Close ticket after confirmation from Lumina Health that alerts are firing for their embedded pages and after 48h of monitoring on the new metric tile. Create public KB article describing embedding caveats if pattern recurs.
